claims.explanation: Triciribine is an AKT inhibitor, and its selective killing pattern is best explained by dependence on PI3K/AKT pathway activation. Sensitive lines frequently have mutations that activate this pathway (e.g., PIK3CA, PTEN loss, EGFR, MET, BRAF, NRAS) or are known to be AKT-dependent, while resistant lines often lack such alterations or have mutations in other pathways. The virtual cell response showing mTOR inhibitor-like transcriptional changes further supports AKT/mTOR pathway inhibition as the mechanism.

features.basis: PTEN loss activates AKT; sensitive lines include ZR751, HEC265, and literature shows triciribine restores sensitivity in PTEN-deficient cells
Activating PIK3CA mutations drive AKT signaling; observed in sensitive lines HGC27, SNU840, MKN1 (though MKN1 resistant, overall pathway activation)
High AKT1 expression increases dependence on AKT signaling; triciribine targets AKT1
High AKT2 expression increases dependence on AKT signaling; triciribine targets AKT2
High AKT3 expression increases dependence on AKT signaling; triciribine targets AKT3
EGFR mutations activate PI3K/AKT; observed in sensitive lines KYSE270, HCC4006
MET amplification/mutation activates PI3K/AKT; observed in sensitive line HGC27
BRAF mutations can activate AKT via ERK crosstalk; observed in sensitive lines LOXIMVI, HEC265, K029AX
NRAS mutations activate PI3K/AKT; observed in sensitive lines IPC298, KU1919
NF1 loss hyperactivates RAS/PI3K/AKT; observed in sensitive lines LOXIMVI, BICR6, S117
FBXW7 mutations are common in resistant lines (NCIH1648, MKN1, SNUC5) and may reduce AKT dependence
STK11 mutations observed in resistant lines KALS1 and SNU840 (though SNU840 sensitive, overall trend)
